evals.name: plugin manifest owner
evals.prompt: A user asks: audit src/.agentbundler/packages/discovery.json for skill grouping, generated export risk, and whether its agents fit its skills. Describe the workflow and output.
evals.expected_output: The response treats package JSON as an AI-agent configuration manifest, inventories the source/generated surfaces, checks plugin grouping and role envelopes, proposes the smallest config fix, and verifies with build/validate checks.
assertions: The output treats src/.agentbundler/packages/discovery.json as config or plugin manifest scope.
The output checks whether listed agents can support the plugin's skills or fix mode.
The output considers source-to-generated export correctness and avoids editing generated output as source.
The output proposes scoped config fixes rather than instruction-score findings.
The output includes validation such as make validate, make build, or generated drift checks.

evals.name: audit config latest features
evals.prompt: A user says: evolve my Claude Code configuration and check whether we are up to date. Describe the workflow.
evals.expected_output: The response audits current config, researches/latest-features when needed, compares against best practices, proposes scoped changes, and verifies generated config.
assertions: The output inventories current Claude Code configuration before proposing changes.
The output checks latest features or best practices rather than relying only on memory.
The output compares current setup against concrete opportunities or anti-patterns.
The output proposes scoped config changes instead of broad rewrites.
The output includes validation or verification after changes.

evals.name: avoid unrequested rewrite
evals.prompt: A user asks: are there any small improvements to my config? Describe how to avoid overreach.
evals.expected_output: The response limits scope to audit and small recommendations, asks before major changes, preserves working configuration, and separates must-fix from optional improvements.
assertions: The output limits itself to small improvements or an audit unless the user approves more.
The output preserves working configuration and avoids wholesale rewrites.
The output separates must-fix issues from optional suggestions.
The output asks for confirmation before making major or risky config changes.
The output includes a way to verify config changes if applied.

evals.name: review claude config scope
evals.prompt: A user asks: review my Claude Code setup, skills, agents, and hooks for context waste and anti-patterns. Describe the workflow.
evals.expected_output: The response treats this as configuration review, inventories skills/agents/hooks/settings, checks trigger quality and context efficiency, cites files, and produces prioritized findings.
assertions: The output treats the task as Claude Code configuration review rather than normal source-code review.
The output inventories relevant configuration such as skills, agents, hooks, settings, or AGENTS/CLAUDE files.
The output checks context efficiency, signal density, trigger quality, or anti-patterns.
The output cites concrete file paths or configuration locations for findings.
The output prioritizes findings and gives actionable fixes.

evals.name: skill trigger boundary review
evals.prompt: A user says several skills trigger at the wrong time. Describe how to audit and improve the configuration without editing yet.
evals.expected_output: The response reviews descriptions/triggers for overlap, too broad/too narrow wording, neighboring skill boundaries, and proposes concrete trigger changes with verification examples.
assertions: The output checks skill descriptions or trigger text for being too broad, too narrow, or overlapping.
The output compares neighboring skill boundaries rather than reviewing each skill in isolation.
The output proposes concrete trigger wording or boundary fixes before implementation.
The output includes example prompts or scenarios to verify activation behavior.
The output avoids editing until the proposed scope is clear or approved.
